summary.oneLiner: Patel Integrated Logistics crossed the INR 10 crore PAT milestone in FY26 driven by a strategic shift to high-margin air freight and disciplined cost control, while launching an asset-light trucking subsidiary to improve ROCE. Management signals imminent valuation rerating via non-core property redevelopment and a 30% dividend payout, leveraging a net-debt-free balance sheet to capitalize on India's airport expansion.

one-line thesis: Patel Integrated Logistics crossed the INR 10 crore PAT milestone in FY26 driven by a strategic shift to high-margin air freight and disciplined cost control, while launching an asset-light trucking subsidiary to improve ROCE. Management signals imminent valuation rerating via non-core property redevelopment and a 30% dividend payout, leveraging a net-debt-free balance sheet to capitalize on India's airport expansion.
financial scorecard: Revenue: INR 96.74cr (Q4, +11.68% YoY), INR 357.25cr (FY26); EBITDA/Margin: Not explicitly stated, but PBT surged 99% QoQ to INR 3.70cr (Q4) and 34% YoY to INR 10.30cr (FY26); PAT: INR 2.98cr (Q4, +60% YoY), INR 9.58cr (FY26, +26% YoY); Order Book: Not disclosed (spot/contract mix implied); Net Debt: Net cash positive (>INR 20cr cash), technically debt-free with minimal operational debt; One-offs: Finance costs dropped sharply to INR 0.35cr from INR 1.18cr prior year.
guidance: Revenue growth: Rajpat Logistics expected to add ~25% to current INR 400cr run-rate over 2-3 years; Margin: Targeting >15% ROCE in new trucking vertical; Order inflow: Benefiting from hardening international air freight rates (+15% since March); Capex/Commissioning: No asset-heavy capex planned; asset-light model only.
order book & pipeline: Not explicitly quantified; management cites strong momentum from 60+ airline partnerships and hardening rates driving revenue despite volume uncertainties.
segment / subsidiary detail: Air Freight: Profit rose to INR 11.26cr (FY26) from INR 8.53cr; operates in 100 airports serving pharma, auto, electronics, FMCG. Rajpat Logistics: New subsidiary for corporate trucking, asset-light (outsourced fleet), targeting minimal receivables and high capital churn.
growth verticals / optionality: Expansion of airport infrastructure (target 220 airports); fleet growth in passenger aircraft (700 to 1800) increasing belly cargo capacity; Rajpat Logistics scaling to INR 100cr+ revenue; Potential recurring income from non-core property redevelopment rather than one-off sale.
margins & cost dynamics: Finance costs reduced by ~70% YoY; rate hardening (+15% international rates) offsetting ATF/crude price pressures; focus on ROCE over gross margin in new verticals.
capex / expansion: Zero asset-heavy capex; strategy remains strictly asset-light (no truck ownership, no immediate warehousing acquisition unless ROCE exceeds current ops).
capital allocation: Final dividend of INR 0.40/share (30% of PAT); cash reserves (>INR 20cr) reserved for operational flexibility and potential property redevelopment participation.
risks & watch-items: Geopolitical tensions affecting ATF prices and capacity; reliance on passenger aircraft belly cargo; execution risk in new Rajpat Logistics vertical; property redevelopment timeline uncertainty.
management quality / tone: Highly confident, emphasizing 'profitable growth,' 'disciplined capital allocation,' and undervaluation; proactive on technology (AI for leakage/receivables) and shareholder returns.
non-obvious takeaways: Management explicitly rejects warehousing expansion unless ROCE exceeds current asset-light returns; property redevelopment likely to be structured for recurring income/participation rather than a one-off asset sale to maximize long-term value; automated system halts credit to customers exceeding risk thresholds without manual intervention.
challenges → beneficiaries & losers:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Hardening air freight rates and capacity constraints due to geopolitical tension and ATF prices | Patel Integrated Logistics Ltd | beneficiary | High | As an organized player with 60+ airline ties, they pass through rate hikes (+15% observed) while smaller unorganized players struggle with capacity; net debt-free status insulates from financing stress. |
| Inefficient capital deployment in traditional asset-heavy logistics | Patel Integrated Logistics Ltd | beneficiary | Med | Shift to asset-light trucking (Rajpat) and avoidance of low-ROCE warehousing could re-rate the stock if >15% ROCE targets are met. |

themes.title: Logistics, ports & supply-chain formalization
themes.need: E-commerce, quick-commerce and GST-driven warehousing consolidation plus a 1P->3P shift drive an integrated-logistics up-cycle. DELHIVERY hit early FCF (>1B parcels, Express +46% rev) with Express targeting 16-18% margin; CONCOR/GATEWAY/JSWINFRA on rail/ports; ALLCARGO/MAHLOG/TVSSCS/VRLLOG on 3PL/road; BLUEDART/TCIEXP/WCIL/SNOWMAN on express + cold-chain; DELHIVERY/SHADOWFAX on quick-commerce fulfilment. Q1FY27's clearest turnaround datapoint: MAHLOG swung to a +INR 25.4cr PAT from a -INR 10.8cr loss on +23% revenue, with B2B Express (Rivigo) gross margin turning +6% from -3.8% and its EBITDA loss cut to -INR 1.6cr from -INR 11.8cr, guided to EBITDA breakeven within FY27, while Contract Logistics grew 26% with margin diluted only ~46bps on new-site start-up costs (opening a site almost every week).
themes.driver: Express/quick-commerce volume momentum; warehousing leasing; port/rail throughput; operating-leverage inflection.
